message.content: {"ranking": [{"id": "patch_c9c4ad33c838", "mechanism": "Replace 0 with w_data in the passthrough o_data assignment, using the available staging wire that carries the buffered data"}, {"id": "patch_926f4e9c3561", "mechanism": "Replace 0 with w_data in the NET_OUTPUT combinational o_data logic, using the available staging wire that carries the buffered data"}, {"id": "patch_1f207853dea8", "mechanism": "Replace 0 with i_data in the REG_OUTPUT sequential o_data logic, directly feeding the input when buffer is empty"}, {"id": "patch_6b523645a71e", "mechanism": "Replace 0 with i_data in the passthrough o_data assignment, directly feeding the input when buffer is empty"}, {"id": "patch_e9c2e7485e9b", "mechanism": "Replace 0 with w_data in the REG_OUTPUT sequential o_data logic, using the staging wire that carries buffered data"}, {"id": "patch_624c3db76fc0", "mechanism": "Replace 0 with i_data in the passthrough o_data assignment, directly feeding the input when buffer is empty"}, {"id": "patch_30270cbdad9d", "mechanism": "Add (!i_valid) gate to r_valid set condition to prevent setting valid when input is not asserted"}, {"id": "patch_df9a5ce60bcb", "mechanism": "Add (i_reset) gate to r_valid clear condition to make clear synchronous with reset"}], "explanation": "The o_data output is stuck at 0 because multiple combinational and sequential assignments drive 0 instead of the correct data sources. The highest-priority fixes directly target the failing o_data assignments by substituting the appropriate data signals (w_data or i_data) for the hardcoded 0. The passthrough path and both output register configurations (NET_OUTPUT and REG_OUTPUT) each have sites where 0 is assigned to o_data. Structural coverage shows these are the exact failure targets. Lower-priority condition_gate patches adjust r_valid control logic but don't directly fix the data path driving o_data=0."}
